info.title: Fel's Voice Lab HTTP API
info.summary: The local service behind the Voice Lab's pages, for scripts and other programs.
info.description: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only. JSON in, JSON out, except where a call returns audio. Every error is a JSON object with an `error` message. See docs/API.md for the conventions, the speaking calls and the command-line tool.

tags.name: Service
tags.description: Is it running, what is loaded, which engines exist. None of these makes audio, except an engine check.

tags.name: Speaking
tags.description: Turn text into audio. `speak` and `performance` answer with the finished WAV file in one response.

tags.name: Cast
tags.description: Characters, the voices (identities) they speak with, the recordings that clone those voices, and pronunciations. Retiring blocks new use of an item and everything made from it; purging deletes it.

tags.name: Takes
tags.description: Saved performances. Every `performance` call and every scene render saves a take with its text, settings, model and provenance. An edit of a take (a trim, a cut of the silence, fades, a gain) is saved as a new take that names its original.

tags.name: Scenes
tags.description: Ordered scripts rendered line by line through the same performance call. The manifest's fields are in [scene-schema-v1.md](scenes/scene-schema-v1.md).

tags.name: Exports
tags.description: Delivery packages: a scene's selected takes, converted, checked and written to `out/exports`.

tags.name: Comparisons
tags.description: Listening comparisons and blind A/B sessions. See [evaluation-schema-v1.md](evaluation/evaluation-schema-v1.md).

tags.name: Conversion
tags.description: Voice conversion: say a recording again in another voice.

tags.name: System
tags.description: The service's report, folder sizes, library backups and housekeeping.

get.summary: Say whether the service is ready, and which version it is.

200.description: `status` (`ready`, or `busy` while a model loads or generates), `busy`, `device`, `version`, `workers` (one entry per loaded engine), `last_worker_error` and `last_unload`.

get.summary: Name the device, the loaded engines, the Kokoro and Phonon voices found and the free memory.

200.description: `device`, `loaded` (the engines in memory), `voices` (Kokoro voice names), `kokoro_languages`, `phonon_voices` (the installed Phonon voices, each with `name`, `group`, `character`, `gender`, `age`, `locale` and `description`) and `free_ram_gb`.

get.summary: List every engine the Lab knows, with its pinned checkpoint, capabilities and license.

200.description: The engine catalog. An engine's `id` is the `engine` of the speaking calls; only engines whose `integration.service_api` is true answer them.

get.summary: Say which engines are installed and usable here, and what each check measured. Reads files and stored results only.

200.description: `device` (the service's: `cuda` for a graphics card, or `cpu`), `busy`, `engines` (one row per catalog engine: `id`, `name`, `integrated`, `installation`, `state`, `check`, `check_outdated`, `min_free_ram_gb`, `device` and, for an integrated engine, `switch`, `device_choice` and `gpu`), `ram`, `install`, `speed` and `store_error`. `installation` holds `installed`, `missing` (the files not found), `environment`, `checkpoint` and, while files are missing from an engine that has a guided installer, `installer`: the launcher in the lab folder that installs it. `min_free_ram_gb` is the free RAM in GB the Lab wants before it loads the engine (`null` when none is set), and `ram` is this computer's `total_gb` and `free_gb`. An engine's `device` is the one its worker is asked for, and `check` is its last check there. `switch` is what its GPU/CPU switch shows (`gpu` or `cpu`), `device_choice` the choice kept for it (`null` when it follows the service), and `gpu` holds `choosable` (GPU can be picked), `reason` (why not), `build` (the PyTorch build in its environment: `cuda`, `rocm`, `cpu` or `null`) and `install` (Install puts in its GPU build). An engine that is not installed and has a guided installer also has `install_size`: `download_bytes` and `disk_bytes` for a first install of the build its Install puts in, from the installer's own numbers (its plan gives the exact figure), or `null` when they cannot be read. `install` is the latest install started from the Models page, or `null` when none has run since the service started: `engine`, `name`, `nvidia` (the GPU build), `state` (`running`, `finished` or `failed`), `started_at`, `ended_at`, `seconds`, `exit_code`, `lines` (the end of its output) and `log` (all of it, a path under the lab folder).

post.summary: Check that one engine can speak now: confirm its files, load it and speak one short clip.

200.description: `check`: `status` (`passed`, `failed` or `not_installed`), `device`, `ran_on`, `checked_at`, `reason`, `load_seconds`, `total_s`, `audio_seconds`, `real_time_factor` and, for a missing install, `missing`. Takes seconds to minutes; the result is kept and shows in `GET /api/engines/status`.

400.description: The engine is unknown, or is not a speech engine.

post.summary: Install an engine with its guided installer (every engine in the catalog has one): read its plan, or run the installer.

dry_run.description: Only read the plan: what the installer would do and whether this computer can take it. Nothing is changed. Default false, which starts the install.

nvidia.description: Install the engine's GPU build for this computer's graphics card (its installer's `--gpu`): NVIDIA's CUDA build, or AMD's ROCm build on a computer whose card is an AMD Radeon. An engine installed with the CPU build of PyTorch can get it afterwards. The Qwen3-TTS models, VoxCPM2 and Breeze TTS 2 run only on a graphics card and always get the GPU build, whatever this says. Default false.

200.description: With `dry_run`, `plan`: `engine`, `nvidia`, `ok`, `paragraphs` (the plan, one string for each paragraph or numbered step) and `problems` (why it cannot go ahead; empty when `ok`). Otherwise `install`: the job that started, as in `GET /api/engines/status`, which is the route to poll for its progress. The job runs the script the engine's launcher runs, with `--yes`. While it runs the service refuses every other load, check and clip.

400.description: The engine is unknown, has no installer (or no GPU build) in the app, or is installed already; or `dry_run` or `nvidia` is not true or false.

409.description: An install is already running, or the GPU worker is busy.

post.summary: Run one engine on the graphics card or on the CPU from its next load, as the switch on its Models & features card does.

200.description: `device`: `engine`, `choice`, `device` (the one its worker is now asked for, `cuda` or `cpu`) and `unloaded` (true when the engine was loaded, so its next request loads it again). The choice is kept in `data/engines/devices.json`. An engine whose environment holds the CPU build of PyTorch runs on the CPU whatever is chosen, until its GPU build is installed.

400.description: The engine is unknown or runs only on the CPU (Phonon, Drama 3), `device` is not `gpu` or `cpu`, or `gpu` was asked of a service that runs on the CPU.

post.summary: Load an engine into memory ahead of its first use.

profile.description: Breeze only: its decode profile. Default `eager`.

200.description: `engine`, `loaded`, `load_seconds`, `sample_rate`, `memory`, `backend`, `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_revision`, `supported_speakers` and `supported_languages`.

500.description: The engine could not load or run. When it is not installed and has a guided installer, `error` begins by saying where to install it: Install on its Models & features card, or its launcher in the lab folder with the arguments that choose the model: `setup-kokoro.bat`, `setup-phonon.bat`, `setup-chatterbox.bat` (Chatterbox Turbo, or with `--original` Chatterbox 500M and Voice Conversion), `setup-qwen.bat` with `--model` and the Qwen3-TTS model, `setup-voxcpm.bat`, `setup-breeze.bat` or `setup-drama3.bat`.

post.summary: Unload every engine and free the GPU.

200.description: `{"ok": true}`.

post.summary: Prepare a reference recording for an engine so its first clone is quick.

engine.description: An engine id that clones from a recording.

path.description: A recording inside the Lab's reference storage.

reference_text.description: The exact transcript, which Breeze, Qwen Base and Drama 3 need.

exaggeration.description: Chatterbox: how strongly to act. Default 0.5.

xvec_only.description: Qwen Base only: use the speaker embedding alone, without a transcript.

200.description: What the engine reports about the prepared reference.

get.summary: Describe the settings each engine's performance takes, and the languages its picker offers.

200.description: `engines`: for each engine its controls (name, type, range, default), whether it takes a direction, and its `languages`; and `unscreened_languages`: per engine, the languages the language screen did not clear.

get.summary: Return this API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document.

200.description: The same document as `openapi.json` in the program folder, built from the route table.

post.summary: Speak text with one engine and answer with the finished WAV file.
post.description: Send no query string: `/api/speak?x=1` is a 404. Qwen, VoxCPM2 and Drama 3 refuse a field they do not take and name it in the 400. To keep what you generate as a Cast take, use [`POST /api/performance`](#post-api-performance).

engine.description: An engine id from `GET /api/catalog` whose `integration.service_api` is true. Default `kokoro`.

voice.description: Kokoro: a voice name, or several joined with commas to blend them. Default `af_heart`. Phonon: one voice name from `phonon_voices` of `GET /api/info`. Default `Harper`.

language.description: Kokoro and Qwen: the language. Default `English`. Phonon speaks English only.

voice_description.description: Qwen VoiceDesign, VoxCPM2 and Breeze design mode: the voice to invent, in words.

mode.description: For engines with several modes: `design`, `clone`, `continuation`, `custom_voice` or, for Breeze, `direction`. A checkpoint accepts the modes it supports.

reference_path.description: Cloning: a recording inside the Lab's reference storage.

reference_text.description: Cloning: the exact transcript of that recording.

direction.description: Engines with a direction control: how to deliver the line, up to 1000 characters.

seed.description: Engines that take one: the random seed. Default 42.

temperature.description: Phonon: how much the delivery varies, 0 to 1. Default 0.3. The other engines that take a temperature list theirs under `capabilities` in `GET /api/catalog`.

duration_delta.description: Phonon: shift the pace, from -0.5 (faster) to 0.5 (slower). Default 0.

save_voice_as.description: Design mode only: keep the invented voice as a reusable reference under this name, letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to two folders deep.

200.description: The whole 16-bit WAV file, in one response with a `Content-Length`. The call blocks until the clip is finished; there is no streaming and no partial answer. Other engine-specific fields are listed under each engine's `capabilities` in `GET /api/catalog`.

X-Audio-Seconds.description: Seconds of audio in the file.

X-First-Chunk.description: Seconds to the first audio, when the engine reports it; otherwise empty.

X-Generation-Mode.description: The mode the engine ran in, when it reports one.

X-Checkpoint-Revision.description: The checkpoint's pinned revision, when reported.

X-Voice-Asset-Path.description: With `save_voice_as`: the file the voice was saved to.

409.description: `save_voice_as` names a voice that already exists, or the GPU worker is busy with another request. One generation runs at a time; a second request is refused, not queued.

500.description: The engine could not load or run. When it is not installed and has a guided installer, `error` begins by saying where to install it: Install on its Models & features card, or its launcher in the lab folder with the arguments that choose the model: `setup-kokoro.bat`, `setup-phonon.bat`, `setup-chatterbox.bat` (Chatterbox Turbo, or with `--original` Chatterbox 500M and Voice Conversion), `setup-qwen.bat` with `--model` and the Qwen3-TTS model, `setup-voxcpm.bat`, `setup-breeze.bat` or `setup-drama3.bat`.

504.description: The engine did not answer in time.

post.summary: Speak text with a Qwen3-TTS checkpoint and stream the audio as it is made.
post.description: Use `POST /api/speak` when you want a file.

voice_description.description: VoiceDesign: the voice to invent, in words.

reference_path.description: Base (clone): a recording inside the Lab's reference storage.

speaker.description: CustomVoice: a speaker the loaded checkpoint reports.

save_voice_as.description: VoiceDesign only: keep the voice as a reusable reference under this name.

200.description: Newline-delimited JSON: one `start` line, `audio` lines (`sequence`, `sample_start`, `sample_count`, `sample_rate`, `sample_format` `pcm_s16le` and the PCM as base64 in `data`) and a closing `complete` line with the timings. A failure after the first line arrives as an `error` line, not a status code.

post.summary: Speak a line as a Cast voice and save it as a take.
post.description: See [Speak as a Cast voice](#speak-as-a-cast-voice) for how to find the ids and what a retry does.

identity_id.description: The voice identity to speak with, from `GET /api/cast`.

line_id.description: Your own label for the line, 1 to 100 characters. Takes are grouped by voice and line.

reference_version_id.description: The recording to clone from. Default: the identity's approved recording. Refused for a fixed or preset voice.

language.description: Default: the voice's own language, else `English`.

direction.description: How to deliver the line, up to 1000 characters. An engine with no verified direction control refuses a non-empty one.

use_pronunciations.description: Apply the character's pronunciation dictionary to the spoken text. The take keeps both texts. Default false.

idempotency_key.description: 1 to 200 characters. Repeating a call with the same key and the same inputs returns that take's audio without generating again.

identity_snapshot.description: Used by scene batches: the voice's `identity_type`, `engine_id` and `engine_options` as the scene saved them. The call is refused if the voice has changed since.

200.description: The take's 16-bit WAV file, in one response. The call blocks until the clip is finished and saved.

X-Audio-Seconds.description: Seconds of audio in the file.

X-Idempotent-Replay.description: `true` when the answer is an earlier take for the same key; then only `X-Take-Id` and the three `X-Cast-*` headers come with it.

400.description: The identity is rejected or retired, has no usable recording, the text or direction is too long, the settings do not fit the engine, or `idempotency_key` was used before with different inputs or for an edit of a take.

404.description: The identity or the recording does not exist.

409.description: The GPU worker is busy. One generation runs at a time; a second request is refused, not queued.

504.description: The engine did not answer in time.

post.summary: Show the phonemes Kokoro would speak for a text.
post.description: Kokoro's language rules live in its own environment, so its worker answers: Kokoro is loaded first when it is not loaded already, as for speaking, and the model loaded before it is unloaded. A text or a language it cannot take is refused with a 400 before anything loads.

200.description: `language`, `language_name` and `segments`, each with its `graphemes` and `phonemes`.

get.summary: List every character with its voices and their recordings.

200.description: `schema_version` and `characters`. Each character has `id`, `name`, `description`, `tags` and `identities`; each identity has `id`, `engine_id`, `label`, `status` (`candidate`, `approved` or `rejected`), `kind` (`reference`, `fixed_voice` or `preset_voice`), `engine_options`, `approved_reference_id`, `notes` and `references` (the recordings, newest version first, each with `id`, `version`, `transcript`, `origin`, `allowed_use`, `duration_seconds` and `audio_url`). Retired items say so.

post.summary: Create a character.
Rename a character or change its description.

name.description: 1 to 80 characters. Leave out to keep it.

description.description: Up to 2000 characters. Leave out to keep it.

200.description: `character`.

post.summary: Add a voice to a character.
post.description: A cloning voice has no recording yet: upload one with [`POST /api/identities/{identity_id}/references`](#post-api-identities-identity_id-references).

engine_id.description: A recording-cloning engine, `kokoro`, `phonon-31m-en` or the Qwen CustomVoice engine that the service exposes.

voice.description: Kokoro: a voice name, or several joined with commas to blend them. Default `af_heart`.

speaker.description: CustomVoice: a speaker the loaded checkpoint reports. Phonon: a voice name from `phonon_voices` of `GET /api/info`.

language.description: CustomVoice: a language the loaded checkpoint reports. Phonon: `English`, the default.

default_direction.description: CustomVoice: the delivery instruction to use when a line gives none.

201.description: `identity`. A new voice is a `candidate` until it is approved.

post.summary: Rename a voice, change its notes or Kokoro voice, or approve or reject it.
post.description: Approving a cloning voice needs a recording with its exact transcript. Approving a voice sends another approved voice of the same character and engine back to `candidate`.

reference_version_id.description: The recording to approve; needed to approve a cloning voice.

200.description: `identity`.

post.summary: Upload a recording for a cloning voice and save it as a reference version.
post.description: Send the recording's bytes as the body (WAV, FLAC, Ogg, MP3 or M4A) and, in the `X-Reference-Metadata` header, base64url-encoded JSON: `{"filename": "nell.wav", "transcript": "...", "origin": "...", "allowed_use": "...", "edits": {"start_seconds": 0.5, "end_seconds": 9.0, "target_sample_rate": 24000, "channel": "mono", "noise_reduction": {"enabled": false}}}`. `filename` sets the format; `edits` is optional. The saved reference is 0.5 to 60 seconds.

201.description: `reference`: the saved version with its quality readings and `audio_url`.

post.summary: Process a recording the way an upload would, and return the result without saving anything.
post.description: Same body and `X-Reference-Metadata` header as the upload.

200.description: The processed WAV. Its quality readings are in the `X-Reference-*` headers.

X-Reference-Quality.description: Base64url-encoded JSON of the quality assessment.

post.summary: Save a take as a new reference recording for a cloning voice.

edits.description: Trim, rate and channel edits, as for an upload.

origin.description: Default: a note naming the take.

allowed_use.description: Added to the take's own terms, which always carry over.

post.summary: Save a new version of a reference recording with a different transcript or trim.

transcript.description: Up to 1200 characters. Default: the current one.

start_seconds.description: Trim start in the source recording.

parameters.name: reference_id
parameters.description: A reference recording version's id, from `GET /api/cast`.

201.description: `reference`: the new version. The earlier one is kept as it was.

get.summary: Download a reference version's processed WAV.

parameters.name: reference_id
parameters.description: A reference recording version's id, from `GET /api/cast`.

200.description: The WAV.

get.summary: Download the recording a reference version was made from.

parameters.name: reference_id
parameters.description: A reference recording version's id, from `GET /api/cast`.

200.description: The recording as it was uploaded.

post.summary: Draft a transcript of a reference recording. Nothing is saved.

parameters.name: reference_id
parameters.description: A reference recording version's id, from `GET /api/cast`.

200.description: `suggestion`: the drafted text and how it was made. Check it before saving it with a new version.

get.summary: List pronunciation entries.

parameters.name: character_id
parameters.description: A character's entries together with the shared ones. Default: only the shared ones.

200.description: `pronunciations`: `id`, `character_id` (null when shared), `source`, `replacement`, `notes`.

post.summary: Add a pronunciation, or change the one with the same term.

replacement.description: How to spell it for the engine, 1 to 200 characters.

200.description: `pronunciation`.

post.summary: Retire a character, voice, recording or take: block new use of it and of everything made from it. Nothing is deleted.

201.description: `retirement` and `affected`: how many items of each kind it reaches.

post.summary: Lift a retirement.

200.description: `{"restored": true}`. Something retired because it came from a retired source stays blocked until that source is restored.

get.summary: Show what purging a retired item would delete.

200.description: `would_purge` (counts by kind), `media_files` and `external_copies`: copies of the audio outside Cast storage, which a purge lists but never deletes.

post.summary: Permanently delete a retired item, everything made from it, and their audio.

confirm.description: Must be `true`; anything else is refused.

200.description: `batch_id`, `purged` (counts by kind), `media_files` and `external_copies`.

400.description: The item is not retired, `confirm` is not `true`, or a file could not be removed (nothing is purged then, so the call can be repeated).

get.summary: List takes, oldest first.

200.description: `takes`: each with `id`, `character_id`, `character_name`, `identity_id`, `identity_label`, `engine_id`, `reference_version_id`, `line_id`, `text`, `spoken_text`, `language`, `direction`, `settings`, `model`, `provenance`, `sample_rate`, `duration_seconds`, `status`, `rating`, `notes`, `created_at`, `loudness`, `waveform_checks`, `has_word_timings`, `has_phoneme_timings`, `parent_take_id` and `edit` (null unless the take is an edit of another take), `audio_url` and its retirement state.

get.summary: Read one take.

parameters.name: take_id
parameters.description: A take's id: the `X-Take-Id` header of a performance, or an entry of `GET /api/takes`.

200.description: `take`, as in `GET /api/takes`.

get.summary: Download a take's WAV.

parameters.name: take_id
parameters.description: A take's id: the `X-Take-Id` header of a performance, or an entry of `GET /api/takes`.

200.description: The WAV.

get.summary: Draw a take: its peaks, its level and where the speech is.

parameters.name: take_id
parameters.description: A take's id: the `X-Take-Id` header of a performance, or an entry of `GET /api/takes`.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: How many slices to summarise the take in, 10 to 2000. Default 600.

200.description: `duration_seconds`, `sample_rate`, `points`, `peaks` (a `[min, max]` pair from -1 to 1 for each slice), `peak_dbfs` and `rms_dbfs` (null for silence), and `speech`: the part louder than -50 dB, with its `start_seconds` and `end_seconds`, or null when nothing is.

400.description: `points` is not a whole number from 10 to 2000, or the stored audio is missing or has changed.

post.summary: Hear an edit of a take without saving anything.
post.description: An edit never changes the take it starts from. The steps run in this order: trim to `start_seconds` to `end_seconds`; auto-trim inside that range (quiet inside the speech is never cut); the two fades, on a raised-cosine curve; then the gain. A trim alone copies the samples exactly; a fade or a gain recalculates them and rounds back to 16 bits. The new take keeps the parent's text, voice, settings and model, starts as a `candidate`, and has its loudness and checks measured again. Its word and phoneme times, when the parent has them, move with the trim, and a word the trim cuts away leaves them. An edit of an edit is allowed. Retiring a take retires its edits, and purging it deletes them.

start_seconds.description: Where the kept part starts, in seconds from the start of the take. Default 0.

end_seconds.description: Where the kept part ends. Default the end of the take. It must be after `start_seconds`.

auto_trim.description: Cut the quiet before and after the speech inside that range. Default false.

silence_threshold_db.description: Auto-trim: anything quieter than this counts as silence, from -90 to -10 dB. Default -50.

keep_silence_ms.description: Auto-trim: how much of the silence to leave at each end, 0 to 2000 ms. Default 80.

fade_in_ms.description: A fade in over the start of the result, 0 to 5000 ms. Default 0.

fade_out_ms.description: A fade out over the end of the result, 0 to 5000 ms. Default 0.

gain_db.description: Make the result louder or quieter, -60 to 24 dB. A gain that would clip is refused. Default 0.

parameters.name: take_id
parameters.description: A take's id: the `X-Take-Id` header of a performance, or an entry of `GET /api/takes`.

200.description: The edited audio as a 16-bit mono WAV. Nothing is saved, and the take is not changed.

X-Audio-Seconds.description: Seconds of audio in the edited clip.

X-Edit-Start-Seconds.description: Where in the take the kept part starts.

X-Edit-End-Seconds.description: Where in the take the kept part ends.

X-Peak-Dbfs.description: The loudest sample of the edited clip in dBFS; empty for silence.

400.description: A field is unknown, not a number (or not true or false) or out of range; `end_seconds` is not after `start_seconds`; the edit changes nothing; the result would be under 0.05 seconds; the two fades are longer than the result; auto-trim finds nothing louder than the threshold; a gain would clip the loudest sample (the answer says how much the take can take); the take is retired; or its stored audio is missing or no longer matches its checksum.

post.summary: Save an edit of a take as a new take.
post.description: An edit never changes the take it starts from. The steps run in this order: trim to `start_seconds` to `end_seconds`; auto-trim inside that range (quiet inside the speech is never cut); the two fades, on a raised-cosine curve; then the gain. A trim alone copies the samples exactly; a fade or a gain recalculates them and rounds back to 16 bits. The new take keeps the parent's text, voice, settings and model, starts as a `candidate`, and has its loudness and checks measured again. Its word and phoneme times, when the parent has them, move with the trim, and a word the trim cuts away leaves them. An edit of an edit is allowed. Retiring a take retires its edits, and purging it deletes them.

start_seconds.description: Where the kept part starts, in seconds from the start of the take. Default 0.

end_seconds.description: Where the kept part ends. Default the end of the take. It must be after `start_seconds`.

auto_trim.description: Cut the quiet before and after the speech inside that range. Default false.

silence_threshold_db.description: Auto-trim: anything quieter than this counts as silence, from -90 to -10 dB. Default -50.

keep_silence_ms.description: Auto-trim: how much of the silence to leave at each end, 0 to 2000 ms. Default 80.

fade_in_ms.description: A fade in over the start of the result, 0 to 5000 ms. Default 0.

fade_out_ms.description: A fade out over the end of the result, 0 to 5000 ms. Default 0.

gain_db.description: Make the result louder or quieter, -60 to 24 dB. A gain that would clip is refused. Default 0.

idempotency_key.description: 1 to 200 characters. Repeating the call with the same key and the same edit returns the take that was made instead of making another.

parameters.name: take_id
parameters.description: A take's id: the `X-Take-Id` header of a performance, or an entry of `GET /api/takes`.

201.description: `take`, the new take as in `GET /api/takes` (its `parent_take_id` is this take and its `edit` says what was done), and `replayed`. A repeat with the same `idempotency_key` answers `200` with `replayed: true` and the take made the first time.

400.description: A field is unknown, not a number (or not true or false) or out of range; `end_seconds` is not after `start_seconds`; the edit changes nothing; the result would be under 0.05 seconds; the two fades are longer than the result; auto-trim finds nothing louder than the threshold; a gain would clip the loudest sample (the answer says how much the take can take); the take is retired; or its stored audio is missing or no longer matches its checksum. An `idempotency_key` used before for a different edit, another take or a performance is refused too.

post.summary: Mark a take selected, rejected or candidate, rate it, or note it.

status.description: `candidate`, `selected` or `rejected`. Selecting a take returns the line's other selected take to `candidate`.

parameters.name: take_id
parameters.description: A take's id: the `X-Take-Id` header of a performance, or an entry of `GET /api/takes`.

200.description: `take`.

get.summary: Score how closely a take's voice matches its reference recording, with the optional speaker model.

target_reference_path.description: The voice to convert to: a WAV, FLAC or Ogg recording of up to 10 seconds in the reference, saved-voice, Cast reference or conversion folders. A file kept with `POST /api/conversion/uploads` must have been sent as a target.

201.description: `conversion`: `conversion_id`, `audio_url`, `audio_path`, `manifest_path` and the manifest, which names both inputs by checksum, and for a file chosen from this computer its original name and, for the target, the origin and allowed use it was given.

post.summary: Keep a recording from this computer as a source performance or a target voice for voice conversion.
post.description: Send the recording's bytes as the body (WAV, FLAC, Ogg, MP3 or M4A) and, in the `X-Reference-Metadata` header, base64url-encoded JSON: `{"filename": "take.mp3", "role": "source"}` for the performance, or `{"filename": "voice.wav", "role": "target", "permission": true, "origin": "...", "allowed_use": "..."}` for the voice to convert to, which is refused without all three. `filename` sets the format and the label, and names nothing on disk: the recording is kept as a mono WAV named by the SHA-256 of the bytes sent, in `out/conversions/uploads/source` or `.../target`, so the same file sent twice is kept once, with a JSON of the rest beside it. A source may be 0.5 to 60 seconds long and a target 0.5 to 10.
